jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord; calm authority, tender with the afflicted, grave in discourse.

man-born-blind.name: The man born blind
man-born-blind.note: Beggar healed at Siloe; plain, increasingly bold and wry before his interrogators, then adoring.

the-jews.name: The Jews
the-jews.note: The Judean authorities and their party; hostile, pressing, sometimes merely onlookers.

pharisees.name: Pharisees
pharisees.note: Strict teachers of the law; censorious, stung.

other-pharisees.name: Other Pharisees
other-pharisees.note: The dissenting Pharisees, puzzled by the miracle.

neighbours.name: Neighbours
neighbours.note: Neighbours of the blind beggar; astonished, curious.

other-neighbours.name: Other neighbours
other-neighbours.note: Neighbours who doubt it is the same man.

parents-of-blind-man.name: Parents of the blind man
parents-of-blind-man.note: His father and mother; frightened, evasive before the authorities.

disciples.name: Disciples
disciples.note: The Twelve; questioning, anxious for their master.

1.t: And Jesus passing by, saw a man who was blind from his birth.

2.t: Rabbi, who hath sinned, this man or his parents, that he should be born blind?

3.t: Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents; but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.

4.t: I must work the works of him that sent me, whilst it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.

5.t: As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.

6.t: When he had said these things, he spat on the ground and made clay of the spittle and spread the clay upon his eyes,

7.t: Go, wash in the pool of Siloe,
which is interpreted, Sent. He went therefore and washed: and he came seeing.

8.t: The neighbours, therefore, and they who had seen him before that he was a beggar, said:
Is not this he that sat and begged?

9.t: No, but he is like him.
9.q: "others" of the neighbours contradict the first; given a second group voice

11.t: That man that is called Jesus made clay and anointed my eyes and said to me: Go to the pool of Siloe and wash. And I went: I washed: and I see.

13.t: They bring him that had been blind to the Pharisees.

14.t: Now it was the sabbath, when Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.

15.t: Again therefore the Pharisees asked him how he had received his sight. But he said to them:
He put clay upon my eyes: and I washed: and I see.

16.t: Some therefore of the Pharisees said:
This man is not of God, who keepeth not the sabbath.
How can a man that is a sinner do such miracles?
16.q: the dissenting Pharisees; second group voice so the division is audible

16.t: And there was a division among them.

17.t: They say therefore to the blind man again:
What sayest thou of him that hath opened thy eyes?

18.t: The Jews then did not believe concerning him, that he had been blind and had received his sight, until they called the parents of him that had received his sight,

19.t: Is this your son, who you say was born blind? How then doth he now see?
19.q: v18 calls the interrogators "the Jews" although they are the Pharisees of v13-17; followed the wording through v34

20.t: His parents answered them and said:
We know that this is our son and that he was born blind:

21.t: But how he now seeth, we know not: or who hath opened his eyes, we know not. Ask himself: he is of age: Let him speak for himself.

22.t: These things his parents said, because they feared the Jews: for the Jews had already agreed among themselves that if any man should confess him to be Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.

23.t: He is of age. Ask himself.
23.q: narrator citing the parents' words again; kept as direct speech

24.t: They therefore called the man again that had been blind and said to him:
Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.

25.t: If he be a sinner, I know not. One thing I know, that whereas I was blind. now I see.

26.t: What did he to thee? How did he open thy eyes?

27.t: I have told you already, and you have heard. Why would you hear it again? Will you also become his disciples?

28.t: They reviled him therefore and said:
Be thou his disciple; but we are the disciples of Moses.

29.t: We know that God spoke to Moses: but as to this man, we know not from whence he is.

30.t: The man answered and said to them:
why, herein is a wonderful thing, that you know not from whence he is, and he hath opened my eyes.

31.t: Now we know that God doth not hear sinners: but if a man be a server of God and doth his, will, him he heareth.

32.t: From the beginning of the world it hath not been heard, that any man hath opened the eyes of one born blind.

33.t: Unless this man were of God, he could not do anything.

34.t: They answered and said to him:
Thou wast wholly born in sins; and dost thou teach us?

35.t: Jesus heard that they had cast him out. And when he had found him, he said to him:
Dost thou believe in the Son of God?

36.t: Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?

37.t: Thou hast both seen him; and it is he that talketh with thee.

38.t: And falling down, he adored him.

39.t: For judgment I am come into this world: that they who see not may see; and they who see may become blind.

40.t: And some of the Pharisees, who were with him, heard: and they said unto him:

41.t: If you were blind, you should not have sin: but now you say: We see. Your sin remaineth.
